title: Backups
intro: nexcrate makes copies of its database: on a schedule, before every change to the structure of the database and when you say so. They lie on the same disk as the database. A copy only becomes a real backup once you download it and keep it somewhere else.
keepHint: This many automatic copies stay, older ones are removed. Copies made by hand stay until you delete them. Automatic copies are made at night between 3 and 6.
folderHint: The copies lie in the folder {{folder}}.

create.title: New backup
create.sub: A copy of the database with the TRaSH state. Cached TMDB answers stay out, they come back by themselves. With a large database this takes a few minutes on a NAS.
create.noteHint: How you will recognise it later, such as "before reworking the profiles". Also part of the file name.

downloadDialog.title: Download backup
downloadDialog.what: You get an encrypted ZIP with the database, the key for the stored credentials and the TRaSH state. 7-Zip and WinRAR open it, the Windows Explorer cannot.
downloadDialog.warning: Without the password the backup is worthless. There is no second key, and nexcrate cannot open the archive either.

delete.title: Delete backup?
delete.warning: This cannot be undone. If you have not downloaded it, this state is gone afterwards.

restoreCopy.title: Restore this copy?
restoreCopy.text: The copy from {{when}} (note: {{note}}) replaces the current database. The key for the stored credentials stays this installation's own.

autoNote.beforeSchemaChange: Before a change of the database
